title: Typhoon Champi Brings Flight Cancellations and Rain Warnings to Taiwan
summaryZh: 颱風羌彼逼近，華航、虎航取消多班沖繩航班，氣象署週五、六影響最大。
summaryHi: तूफ़ान चाम्पी के करीब आने से ताइवान में उड़ानें रद्द, शुक्रवार-शनिवार सबसे ज़्यादा असर।
summaryEs: El tifón Champi se acerca a Taiwán: vuelos cancelados y lluvias el viernes y sábado.
summaryJa: 台風チャンパー接近で台湾の航空便が欠航、金・土曜に影響が最大に。
summaryKo: 태풍 참피 접근으로 대만 항공편 결항, 금·토요일 영향 가장 클 듯.
summaryEn: Typhoon Champi nears Taiwan, cancelling flights; its biggest impact is expected Friday and Saturday.
paragraphs: Typhoon Champi is approaching Taiwan, and several airlines have already cancelled or rescheduled flights. The Central Weather Administration (CWA) expects the storm to have its greatest impact on the island on Friday and Saturday, bringing rain to most areas.

As of 2 p.m. on Wednesday, the typhoon's centre was about 910 kilometres east-southeast of Eluanbi, Taiwan's southernmost point. It was heading north-west at 19 kilometres per hour, with maximum sustained winds of 209 kilometres per hour and a radius of 280 kilometres.

Because the storm's expected path has shifted slightly west, the CWA said a sea warning could be issued late on Wednesday night or early on Thursday, followed by a possible land warning on Thursday afternoon. A forecaster said Champi should weaken as it turns north, before moving towards Japan's Kyushu region on Saturday.

China Airlines and Tigerair Taiwan cancelled a number of Thursday flights linking Taoyuan, Taichung, Kaohsiung and Tainan with Okinawa. Domestic carriers Uni Air and Mandarin Airlines also dropped some flights to the outlying islands of Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu. EVA Air and Starlux said their schedules were unchanged for now, but warned that some services could be affected in the coming days.
Meanwhile, stronger seasonal winds from the north-east are expected to bring cooler weather to northern Taiwan, with daytime highs of around 24 degrees Celsius.
A big storm is coming near Taiwan. Its name is Typhoon Champi.
On Wednesday, the storm was far away in the sea, about 910 kilometres from the south of Taiwan. It was moving north-west.
The weather office says the storm will be strongest in Taiwan on Friday and Saturday. There will be a lot of rain on the island.
Some airlines stopped flights for Thursday. China Airlines and Tigerair Taiwan cancelled many flights to Okinawa in Japan. Small planes to the islands of Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu also stopped.
Other airlines say their flights are normal now. But they tell people to check their flight before they go to the airport. The storm will go to Japan on Saturday.

Typhoon Champi is moving towards Taiwan, and airlines have already started to cancel flights. The Central Weather Administration (CWA) says the storm will affect the island most on Friday and Saturday.

At 2 p.m. on Wednesday, the centre of the typhoon was about 910 kilometres east-southeast of Eluanbi, the most southern point of Taiwan. It was moving north-west at 19 kilometres per hour, with very strong winds of up to 209 kilometres per hour.

The CWA said it might give a sea warning late on Wednesday night or early on Thursday, and a land warning could follow on Thursday afternoon. The storm should become weaker when it turns north, and it will probably leave for Kyushu in Japan on Saturday.

China Airlines and Tigerair Taiwan cancelled several Thursday flights between Taiwan and Okinawa. Uni Air and Mandarin Airlines also cancelled some flights to Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu. EVA Air and Starlux said their flights had not changed yet, but they asked passengers to check before going to the airport.
Northern Taiwan will also feel cooler on Thursday, with highs of about 24 degrees.

As of 2 p.m. on Wednesday, the typhoon's centre was about 910 kilometres east-southeast of Eluanbi, Taiwan's southernmost point. It was heading north-west at 19 kilometres per hour, with maximum sustained winds of 209 kilometres per hour and a radius of 280 kilometres.

Because the storm's expected path has shifted slightly west, the CWA said a sea warning could be issued late on Wednesday night or early on Thursday, followed by a possible land warning on Thursday afternoon. A forecaster said Champi should weaken as it turns north, before moving towards Japan's Kyushu region on Saturday.

China Airlines and Tigerair Taiwan cancelled a number of Thursday flights linking Taoyuan, Taichung, Kaohsiung and Tainan with Okinawa. Domestic carriers Uni Air and Mandarin Airlines also dropped some flights to the outlying islands of Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu. EVA Air and Starlux said their schedules were unchanged for now, but warned that some services could be affected in the coming days.
Meanwhile, stronger seasonal winds from the north-east are expected to bring cooler weather to northern Taiwan, with daytime highs of around 24 degrees Celsius.

Airlines in Taiwan have begun cancelling and rescheduling flights as Typhoon Champi bears down on the region, with the Central Weather Administration (CWA) predicting that the storm will hit the island hardest on Friday and Saturday.

On Wednesday afternoon, the typhoon was centred roughly 910 kilometres east-southeast of Eluanbi, the island's southernmost tip, and was tracking north-west at 19 kilometres per hour. It was packing maximum sustained winds of 209 kilometres per hour, and its radius stretched to some 280 kilometres.

With the projected path edging slightly westward, the CWA indicated that a sea warning might be issued overnight, and a land warning could follow on Thursday afternoon. Forecasters nevertheless expect Champi to lose strength as unfavourable conditions force it to curve northward, and it is likely to head for Kyushu in Japan on Saturday, allowing warnings to be lifted as early as that afternoon.

Disruption has already begun. China Airlines and Tigerair Taiwan scrapped several Thursday services to Okinawa, while Uni Air and Mandarin Airlines cut flights to the outlying islands of Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu. EVA Air and Starlux kept their timetables intact but cautioned that routes to Japan could be hit in the days ahead.
Northern Taiwan, meanwhile, faces a noticeable drop in temperature as seasonal north-easterly winds strengthen.

Typhoon Champi is forcing airlines in Taiwan to cancel and reschedule flights, and meteorologists warn that its most significant impact on the island will be felt on Friday and Saturday, when heavy rain is anticipated across most regions.

According to the Central Weather Administration (CWA), the system was located approximately 910 kilometres east-southeast of Eluanbi at 2 p.m. on Wednesday, travelling north-west at 19 kilometres per hour. With sustained winds of up to 209 kilometres per hour and a radius of 280 kilometres, it is a substantial storm.

A slight westward shift in its projected trajectory prompted the CWA to signal that a sea warning could be issued overnight, potentially followed by a land warning on Thursday afternoon. However, forecasters anticipate that the typhoon will gradually weaken as it veers north towards Kyushu, Japan, which would allow warnings to be lifted by Saturday afternoon.

Transport has inevitably been affected. China Airlines and Tigerair Taiwan cancelled numerous Thursday flights to Okinawa, and domestic carriers suspended some routes to Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu. Other airlines, including EVA Air and Starlux, have maintained their schedules for the time being but have advised travellers to monitor updates closely.
The episode illustrates how vulnerable island transport networks remain to seasonal storms, and why early, accurate forecasting is essential.
